verdict.note: Nothing is dropped or doubled between A and B, but B's two columns are in the wrong order. A is transcribed right column first, then left (folio 10). B is done the other way: its left column (folio 11, 'בזמר/בתרין ירון') comes first. On the scan, B's right column ('הששית קדוש ידים ורגלים') is the one that follows A's 'קודש לחול כנודע', and it ends with the catchword 'בתרין', which opens the left column. So B's text should read 'הששית…' first and 'בזמר ירון…' after it, in both the transcription and the English.
No text is repeated or carried over between A's end and B's start; A's transcription ends with ellipses that may hide missing words, but the scan's handwriting is too small to confirm a drop.

No carry-over, duplication or dropped words across the break: A's English ends on its last transcribed line ('as a servant with his master') and B's English starts at B's first line ('The custom in our city'). Low confidence: the scan resolution is too low to check the boundary lines word by word, and the folio numbers run backwards (A is 117, B is 116), so the leaf order or the transcriptions should be checked against the scans.

Nothing at the A→B break is carried over, repeated or lost: A's English ends on its last line ('in the name of Ramban, of blessed memory'), B's English starts on B's first line ('Among the gatherers of the crown'), and each English text covers its own transcription. Two caveats. First, each scan shows two facing pages; A's hand-written number reads about 183 and B's about 194, so leaves may be missing between them. I couldn't read the folio numbers or catchwords well enough to confirm this, so I haven't reported it as a defect. Second, both transcriptions differ widely from the handwriting in the scans (for example A line 1 reads 'חנוכה' where the scan does not seem to), and A's folio number עח has been pulled into its first line as 'ע"ח'. Those problems affect each whole page, not the break.
